title: Making your case: connectors and polite disagreement
goal: Build a clear spoken or written argument with Swedish connectors, and disagree in the matter-of-fact, polite way Swedes expect.
bekal: you can order an argument with *för det första*, *dessutom*, *däremot*, *följaktligen* and *med andra ord*
you can concede a point and then counter it with *visserligen … men* and *inte … utan*
you can agree, half-agree and disagree without sounding rude
wave: Go back to Unit 8: say *komma fram till*, *hålla med* and *gå ut på* in a sentence each, then front the object the way Dian does here: *Det håller jag med om.*

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Slutseminariet
dialogs.intro: It is the final seminar for Dian's master's thesis on sustainable cities — green spaces and densification in Hammarby sjöstad. As is the custom at Swedish universities, a fellow student is her “opponent”: Viktor, who already opposed her draft in Unit 4, now has to question the finished thesis in front of everyone.

lines.speaker: Viktor:
lines.text: Jag vill börja med att säga att uppsatsen är välskriven och tydligt disponerad.
lines.id: I'd like to start by saying that the thesis is well written and clearly structured.
lines.literal: I want begin with to say that essay-the is well-written and clearly disposed.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Tack, det är snällt sagt.
lines.id: Thank you, that's kind of you.
lines.literal: thanks, it is kindly said.

lines.speaker: Viktor:
lines.text: Däremot är jag inte helt övertygad om din slutsats om grönytorna.
lines.id: However, I'm not entirely convinced by your conclusion about the green spaces.
lines.literal: on-the-other-hand am I not wholly convinced about your conclusion about green-surfaces-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Kan du utveckla det?
lines.id: Could you elaborate on that?
lines.literal: can you develop that?

lines.speaker: Viktor:
lines.text: Visst. Å ena sidan visar du att de boende besöker parkerna oftare än för tio år sedan. Å andra sidan säger siffrorna ingenting om varför.
lines.id: Sure. On the one hand, you show that residents visit the parks more often than ten years ago. On the other hand, the figures say nothing about why.
lines.literal: sure. on one side-the show you that the residing visit parks-the more-often than for ten years since. on other side-the say figures-the nothing about why.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Där har du en poäng. Samtidigt har jag ju intervjuat trettio boende, och de flesta nämner just de nya grönytorna.
lines.id: You have a point there. At the same time, I did interview thirty residents, and most of them mention the new green spaces specifically.
lines.literal: there have you a point. at-the-same-time have I (you-know) interviewed thirty residents, and the most mention exactly the new green-surfaces-the.

lines.speaker: Viktor:
lines.text: Det stämmer, men trettio personer är knappast ett representativt urval.
lines.id: That's true, but thirty people is hardly a representative sample.
lines.literal: it tallies, but thirty persons is hardly a representative selection.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Det håller jag med om. Därför kallar jag det inte en undersökning utan en fallstudie.
lines.id: I agree with that. That's why I don't call it a survey but a case study.
lines.literal: that hold I with about. therefore call I it not an investigation but a case-study.

lines.speaker: Viktor:
lines.text: Okej. Dessutom saknar jag en diskussion om dem som inte har råd att bo kvar i området.
lines.id: OK. Also, I miss a discussion of the people who can't afford to stay in the area.
lines.literal: okay. moreover lack I a discussion about them who not have means to live remaining in area-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Menar du alltså att stadsdelen inte är socialt hållbar?

lines.literal: mean you so that district-the not is socially sustainable?

lines.speaker: Viktor:
lines.text: Inte nödvändigtvis. Jag menar bara att frågan förtjänar ett eget avsnitt.
lines.id: Not necessarily. I just mean the question deserves a section of its own.
lines.literal: not necessarily. I mean only that question-the deserves an own section.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Det är en rimlig invändning. Med andra ord: nästa uppsats blir längre!
lines.id: That's a fair objection. In other words: my next thesis will be longer!
lines.literal: it is a reasonable objection. with other words: next essay becomes longer!

lines.speaker: Viktor:
lines.text: Sammanfattningsvis tycker jag att det är en stark uppsats, trots bristerna.
lines.id: To sum up, I think it's a strong thesis, despite its weaknesses.
lines.literal: summarizingly think I that it is a strong essay, despite shortcomings-the.

notes: **Jag vill börja med att säga att…** — the classic opening of an *opponering*. At Swedish universities every thesis is “opposed” at the final seminar (*slutseminariet*) by a fellow student, and the unwritten rule is to begin with something positive. Notice *börja med att* + base form: “begin by doing”. English uses *by* + *-ing*; Swedish uses *med att* + infinitive.

**Däremot** (**DEH-reh-moot**, stress on the first syllable) marks a contrast with what came before: “however, on the other hand”. It is an adverb, not a conjunction, so when it comes first the verb must follow at once: *Däremot **är** jag…* — never *Däremot jag är*.

**Å ena sidan … å andra sidan** — “on the one hand … on the other hand”. The *å* (**oh**) is an old form of *på* that survives only in a few fixed phrases (*å ena sidan*, *å mina vägnar*). Each half counts as the first element of its sentence, so both trigger inversion: *Å andra sidan **säger** siffrorna…*

**Där har du en poäng** (**po-ENG**) — “you have a point there”. It concedes a detail without giving up the whole argument, which is exactly why it is so common in Swedish discussion. Its cousin *Det ligger något i det* (“there's something in that”) does the same job.

**Det håller jag med om** — the particle verb *hålla med om* from Unit 8, with the object *det* moved to the front for emphasis. The preposition *om* stays behind at the end, just as in English “That I agree with”. Fronting *det* like this is the most natural way to agree in speech.

**Inte nödvändigtvis** — “not necessarily”. Swedish seminar culture values *saklighet*: being matter-of-fact, criticizing the text and never the person. Viktor never says *du har fel*; he says he is *inte övertygad*, that he *saknar* something, that a question *förtjänar ett eget avsnitt*. Dian answers in kind: *en rimlig invändning*, “a fair objection”.

grammars.title: Connectors by function
body: A B2 argument is held together by small signposts. Learn them by the job they do, not alphabetically.

head: Function
Connectors
Say it
Example
rows: **Med andra ord**: nästa uppsats blir längre.

after: The crucial point is word order. Almost all of these are **adverbs**, so when one of them opens the sentence, the verb comes second and the subject third: *Dessutom **saknar jag**…*, *Följaktligen **blev luften**…*. They can also sit in the middle of the sentence, where *inte* would go: *Henrik vill **däremot** ta det stegvis.*

Only the five **conjunctions** *och*, *men*, *eller*, *för* and *utan* leave the word order alone: *…men **trettio personer är** knappast…*. A quick test: if you can put the word in the middle of a sentence (*Jag är **dessutom** trött*), it is an adverb and it inverts.

grammars.title: Agreeing and disagreeing: a politeness scale
body: Swedes rarely say a flat *Du har fel* (“you're wrong”) to anyone outside the family. The middle of the scale is where real discussions happen.

head: Strength
Agreeing
Disagreeing
rows: Det håller jag helt med om. · Precis så.
Det håller jag inte alls med om. · Där har du fel.
Där har du en poäng. · Det ligger något i det.
Jag håller inte riktigt med. · Jag är inte helt övertygad.
Det kan nog stämma. · Jag förstår hur du tänker.
Jag undrar om det verkligen är så. · Är det inte snarare så att…?
Vad grundar du det på? · Finns det belägg för det?

after: *Jag undrar om…* opens a subordinate clause, so BIFF applies: *Jag undrar om urvalet **inte är** för litet.* The negative question is itself a softener — like English “Isn't the sample a bit small?”

The most Swedish move of all is to agree with a detail before disagreeing with the main point: *Där har du en poäng, men…* It signals that you are listening, which matters more in a consensus culture than winning.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Debatten
dialogs.intro: A week later Dian sits in the audience at a student union debate: “Should central Stockholm become car-free?” Sara argues for, Henrik against, and a moderator keeps time.

lines.speaker: Moderatorn:
lines.text: Välkomna till kvällens debatt: ska Stockholms innerstad bli bilfri?
lines.id: Welcome to tonight's debate: should central Stockholm become car-free?
lines.literal: welcome to evening-the's debate: shall Stockholm's inner-city become car-free?

lines.speaker: Sara:
lines.text: Ja. För det första är luften i innerstan fortfarande för dålig.
lines.id: Yes. Firstly, the air in the city center is still too poor.
lines.literal: yes. for it first is air-the in inner-city-the still too bad.

lines.speaker: Sara:
lines.text: För det andra tar parkerade bilar upp en enorm yta. Följaktligen blir det mindre plats för människor.
lines.id: Secondly, parked cars take up an enormous amount of space. Consequently, there's less room for people.
lines.literal: for it second take parked cars up an enormous surface. consequently becomes it less place for people.

lines.speaker: Henrik:
lines.text: Jag förstår resonemanget, men jag håller inte riktigt med.
lines.id: I understand the reasoning, but I don't quite agree.
lines.literal: I understand reasoning-the, but I hold not really with.

lines.speaker: Henrik:
lines.text: Visserligen behöver vi renare luft, men många hantverkare och äldre är beroende av bilen.
lines.id: Admittedly we need cleaner air, but many tradespeople and older people depend on the car.
lines.literal: admittedly need we cleaner air, but many craftsmen and older are dependent of car-the.

lines.speaker: Sara:
lines.text: Ingen vill förbjuda färdtjänst eller leveranser. Tvärtom, de skulle komma fram mycket snabbare.
lines.id: Nobody wants to ban mobility services or deliveries. On the contrary, they'd get through much faster.
lines.literal: nobody wants forbid travel-service or deliveries. on-the-contrary, they would come forward much faster.

lines.speaker: Henrik:
lines.text: Det låter bra i teorin. I praktiken flyttar trafiken bara ut till närförorterna.
lines.id: That sounds good in theory. In practice, the traffic just moves out to the inner suburbs.
lines.literal: it sounds good in theory-the. in practice-the moves traffic-the only out to near-suburbs-the.

lines.speaker: Moderatorn:
lines.text: Sara, vad säger du om det?
lines.id: Sara, what do you say to that?
lines.literal: Sara, what say you about that?

lines.speaker: Sara:
lines.text: Det finns inga belägg för det. I själva verket visar flera studier att en del av trafiken helt enkelt försvinner.
lines.id: There's no evidence for that. In fact, several studies show that part of the traffic simply disappears.
lines.literal: it exists no proofs for that. in very work-the show several studies that a part of traffic-the wholly simply disappears.

lines.speaker: Henrik:
lines.text: Där har du en poäng. Ändå tror jag att vi måste ta det stegvis.
lines.id: You have a point there. Still, I think we have to take it step by step.
lines.literal: there have you a point. still believe I that we must take it step-wise.

lines.speaker: Moderatorn:
lines.text: Så ni är alltså överens om målet, men inte om tempot?
lines.id: So you agree on the goal, but not on the pace?
lines.literal: so you-all are thus agreed about goal-the, but not about tempo-the?

lines.speaker: Henrik:
lines.text: Kort sagt, ja.
lines.id: In short, yes.
lines.literal: short said, yes.

notes: **För det första … för det andra** — “firstly … secondly”, literally “for the first, for the second”. Remember that *rs* melts into a single **sh** sound: **för deh FÖSH-tah**. Both phrases open the sentence, so the verb jumps ahead of the subject: *För det andra **tar** parkerade bilar…*

**Följaktligen** (**FÖL-yahkt-lee-gen**) means “consequently”. It belongs to writing and prepared speech; in a café you would say *så* or *därför* instead. In a debate it sounds deliberately formal, which is exactly the effect Sara wants.

**Visserligen … men** — the Swedish concession pair, like English “admittedly …, but”. You grant your opponent's point in the first half and land your own in the second. *Visserligen* inverts like any adverb: *Visserligen **behöver vi**…*

**Tvärtom** (**tveh-TOM**) — “on the contrary”. It can stand alone, followed by a comma, or sit inside the sentence: *Det är **tvärtom** billigare.* Don't confuse it with *däremot*: *tvärtom* reverses the claim (“the opposite is true”), *däremot* only contrasts two things.

**I själva verket** — “in fact, actually”, literally “in the very work”. It corrects a false impression. Compare *faktiskt* (Svenska 102, Unit 19): *faktiskt* adds mild surprise in speech; *i själva verket* sets the record straight and works in writing too.

**Överens om** — “in agreement about”. *Vi är överens* (we agree) describes a state; *hålla med* is something one person does towards another. The moderator's *Så ni är alltså…* uses *alltså* to sum up: “so, in other words”.

grammars.title: Conceding and correcting: visserligen … men, inte … utan, tvärtom
body: Three patterns let you take your opponent seriously and still win the point. Their word order is worth learning as a chunk.

head: Pattern
What it does
Example
rows: Visserligen är bilen praktisk, men den tar stor plats.
Det är inte en undersökning utan en fallstudie.
adds Y on top of X
Det gäller inte bara luften utan också bullret.
Y is the opposite of what X suggests
De blir inte långsammare. Tvärtom, de kommer fram snabbare.
Y is the more accurate version
Problemet är inte priset. Snarare tiden.

after: **Utan** vs **men**: after a negative, when the second half *replaces* the first, Swedish must use *utan*, not *men*. *Han är inte dum **utan** lat* = “He isn't stupid, he's lazy.” *Han är inte rik, **men** han är lycklig* = “He isn't rich, but (even so) he's happy.” English uses *but* for both, which is why learners mix them up.
With *inte … utan*, the second half usually drops everything it shares with the first: *Det är inte en undersökning utan (det är) en fallstudie.* That ellipsis is what makes the sentence sound crisp.

blocks.text: Swedish schools teach argumentation with a fixed set of labels, and you will meet them in every debate, op-ed and seminar. Knowing the labels helps you hear the structure of what someone is saying.

head: Step
Swedish label
Useful phrases
rows: Jag anser att… · Min utgångspunkt är att…
För det första… · Dessutom… · Ett annat skäl är att…
Men… · Det finns dock inga belägg för att… · Tvärtom…
Följaktligen… · Sammanfattningsvis… · Därför anser jag att…

blocks.text: Notice **dock** (“however”) in the fourth row. It is the written cousin of *däremot* and *men*, and it usually sits in the middle of the sentence, not at the start: *Det finns **dock** inga belägg.* Starting a sentence with *Dock* is possible but sounds stiff.

blocks.title: Three phrases that buy you time
items: *Det är en bra fråga.* — “That's a good question.” (Universal, and honest more often than not.)
*Hur menar du då?* — “What do you mean by that?” Throws the ball back without sounding hostile.
*Om jag förstår dig rätt, menar du att…* — “If I understand you correctly, you mean that…” Restating the other person's view is the strongest politeness signal in a Swedish discussion.

blocks.text: Swedish has a word that sums up the ideal tone of public discussion: **saklig** (**SAHK-lee**), “matter-of-fact, objective”. Its opposite is **osaklig**, and *Nu är du osaklig!* is one of the harshest things you can say in a debate. It means you have stopped talking about the issue and started talking about the person.

items: Criticize the claim, not the speaker: *Argumentet håller inte* rather than *Du har inte tänkt*.
Let people finish. Interrupting (*att avbryta*) is noticed far more than in English-speaking debates; if you must, say *Får jag bara flika in?* (“May I just cut in?”).
Volume does not win. Calm, slightly understated delivery sounds more convincing in Swedish than passion does.
Consensus is a goal, not a defeat. Ending with *Vi är alltså överens om målet* is a good result, not a draw.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Unit 2
items: Unit 2 showed you att-clauses as subjects: *Att han kom var bra.* Argumentation loves them.
Make three: *Att trafiken minskade är ett faktum.* · *Att alla har råd är inte säkert.* · *Att frågan är viktig håller alla med om.*
In each one, the whole att-clause is the first element, so the verb comes straight after it.
